1.explanation:
All three files participate in the sequence of actions that lead to the default attribute being cleared:

• AppendBehavior.js handles the case where you click the append icon on the gateway and create a new intermediate catch event. It eventually issues a create-connection command.  
• DropOnFlowBehavior.js handles the scenario where you drag and drop a Timer Intermediate Catch Event directly onto an existing sequence flow. It too issues modeling commands that modify connections.  
• UnsetDefaultFlowBehavior.js listens for connection-create/connection-update events and automatically unsets the gateway’s defaultFlow property when it detects certain changes to outgoing sequence flows. Because both append and drop actions go through the same connection logic, UnsetDefaultFlowBehavior fires and clears the defaultFlow on the gateway even though the newly created flow is not the default. This is why these files need to be adjusted to prevent the default attribute from being removed in this case.
1.bug_scenario: When you have an exclusive gateway with two outgoing sequence flows (one marked as the default) and you append or drop a Timer Intermediate Catch Event onto the non-default flow (either by dragging a timer event from the palette onto that flow or by using the append handle), the gateway’s “default” attribute on the business object is unexpectedly removed. Visually the default arrow remains, but the BPMN XML no longer contains the defaultFlow reference on the gateway.

2.explanation:
All three of these files play a role in how an intermediate catch event is attached to a sequence flow and how the model is updated:

• AttachEventBehavior.js – orchestrates attaching an event to an existing flow, firing the commands that ultimately split the flow and create new connectors. Any mis-ordering here can leave the gateway’s default flag out of sync.

• DropOnFlowBehavior.js – carries out the actual ‘drop on connection’ logic, splitting the original sequence flow into two and reconnecting the new event in between. In the process it re-wires the outgoing flows on the gateway and may fail to preserve the default reference on the gateway’s business object.

• UnsetDefaultFlowBehavior.js – listens for sequence flow changes and unsets the default attribute when flows are updated. Its hook is too broad and clears the gateway default even when a non-default branch is modified. Together these three behaviors need to be adjusted so that inserting an intermediate catch event on a non-default flow does not clear the gateway’s default attribute.
2.bug_scenario:
When you take an exclusive gateway with two outgoing sequence‐flows (one marked as the default) and drop a Timer Intermediate Catch Event onto the non-default flow, the code splits that flow (to insert the event), and in the process the gateway’s “default” attribute is unexpectedly cleared. Visually the default marker stays on one branch, but the gateway’s default reference is actually removed from the business object.

In short: dropping a timer (or other catch event) onto a non-default outbound flow of an exclusive gateway unsets the gateway’s default flow property.
